title: Confocal Microscopy and Characterization of Synaptic Boutons Associated with Ganglion Neurons
author: Janet R Keast
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bakdics6
materials: Using Zen Black (Zeiss software), batch process Airyscan output to 16-bit 1260 x 1260 pixel images.

steps.title: Configure microscope objective and zoom
steps.instruction: Mount a 60× 1.4 NA oil‑immersion objective on the Zeiss LSM880 and set the digital zoom to 3×.

steps.title: Acquire multi‑channel Airyscan images
steps.instruction: Using the Zeiss LSM880 in Fast Airyscan mode, collect sequential multi‑channel images, averaging four scans per image. If a channel contains photobleaching‑prone labels (e.g., FluoroGold retrograde tracer), image that channel first.

steps.title: Convert Airyscan data to Imaris format
steps.instruction: Process the Airyscan images and export each channel as an Imaris (.ims) file for analysis with the Surface Rendering module.

steps.title: Create neuronal cell‑body mask
steps.instruction: In Imaris, generate a surface for the neuronal cell‑body channel within a defined volume, then adjust parameters (background subtraction, split touching objects, threshold) as needed. Delete all non‑neuronal objects, select all neuronal surfaces, and merge them into a single mask. For pelvic ganglion cell bodies, set surface detail to 0.2 µm.

substeps.instruction: Generate neuronal surface in defined volume.
Adjust background subtraction, split touching objects, and threshold.
Select and merge all neuronal surfaces.

steps.title: Create synaptic bouton mask
steps.instruction: In Imaris, generate a surface for the synaptic‑bouton channel using the same workflow as for the neuron. For pelvic ganglion studies, set surface detail to 0.05 µm.

substeps.instruction: Generate bouton surface in defined volume.

steps.title: Calculate distances and morphology
steps.instruction: Apply the Distance Transformation extension to the neuronal cell‑body and bouton surfaces to obtain the closest distance between the two surfaces, as well as surface area and volume for all rendered objects.

steps.title: Export analysis results
steps.instruction: Export the distance, surface area, and volume data for each channel (neuronal cell body and boutons) to separate Excel files.
